name: ioc-known-bad
description: Known-bad file indicators for common Linux malware (Kinsing, XMRig, libprocesshider, Diicot, hidden-sshd backdoors). Conservative — present == investigate.  Absent keys/paths SKIP, never false-fail.

rules.title: IOC: kdevtmpfsi present (/tmp/kdevtmpfsi)
rules.rationale: kdevtmpfsi is the payload of the Kinsing cryptomining malware — one of the most common Linux server infections.
rules.fix: If you didn't put kdevtmpfsi there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.

rules.title: IOC: kinsing present (/tmp/kinsing)
rules.fix: If you didn't put kinsing there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.

rules.title: IOC: kthrotlds present (/usr/bin/kthrotlds)

rules.title: IOC: libprocesshider.so present (/usr/lib/libprocesshider.so)

rules.fix: If you didn't put libprocesshider.so there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.
